Bangkok = better for professional fighters / stadium access
Chiang Mai = better for beginners and 1-3 month stays
Chiang Mai = authentic atmosphere, community vibe
Bangkok = urban intensity, higher cost, harder for long-stay

gap.description: Zero content across all top results covers (1) the DTV visa as a decision factor in the CM vs BKK comparison — DTV is mentioned in passing at best, never as the reason to choose CM specifically; (2) women's training experience — not a single top-5 result addresses women's experience, safety, female trainers, or beginner women; (3) the suburban/open-air advantage — Hang Dong / open-air camps are invisible (all competitor content focuses on Nimman tourist-belt gyms); (4) real package pricing in THB as a standalone line-item (training + accommodation bundled, not separate). The #1 competitor is the closest but still misses all 4.

weakness: DTV coverage is universally shallow — mentioned as a label, never explained as a CM-specific advantage
Women: completely absent from all top-5 results for this keyword
Pricing: #1 result has data but uses USD ranges that obscure real THB on-the-ground costs
Community/family framing: all competitors use fight-camp language (hard sessions, pads, conditioning) — the 'stay for the family' positioning is an untapped angle
The suburban open-air camp (Hang Dong) as a category is invisible — all comparisons implicitly assume Nimman/city-centre gyms

wildcat_specific_gaps.dtv_visa_angle: DTV visa is the #1 reason to choose CM over BKK for long-stay foreigners — no competitor article frames it this way. Wildcat has full DTV pillar + how-to-apply — this article can be the connector.
wildcat_specific_gaps.women_angle: Not a single top-5 result mentions women. A sidebar section 'Is Chiang Mai good for women?' would capture the PAA question and rank for the sub-topic.
wildcat_specific_gaps.open_air_camp: Wildcat's open-air, garden-and-pool environment in Hang Dong is a unique differentiator — completely absent from SERP. Framing: 'while Bangkok camps are in concrete gyms, CM has open-air pavilions in green countryside'.
wildcat_specific_gaps.beginner_family: All competitors frame the comparison for experienced trainers. Beginner + family/community framing is wide open.
wildcat_specific_gaps.thb_prices: Wildcat can publish real THB prices (training: 400/session, monthly packages: public on site) — more credible than USD estimates from editorial sites.

recommended_angle: Target beginner/intermediate foreigners planning a 1-3 month stay who are weighing CM vs BKK — and use the DTV visa as the deciding factor: 'Chiang Mai wins on cost, climate, community, and now it wins on visa too — DTV lets you stay 180 days and Wildcat handles the paperwork.' Lead with the cost table (real THB), add a women's sidebar, and anchor to the open-air/family atmosphere that no competitor covers.
